Cold pre-dawn blue fills the sky, the colossal ship a darker shape against it, its underside just beginning to glow a soft white.
A single shaft of white light lowers from the dark hull to touch the land, its glow catching drifting dust and low mist.
The low sun rises warm and amber behind the arrival, rimming its dark silhouette in gold, long shadows reaching across the plain.
An eerie teal luminescence suffuses the mist below the visitor, the hull pulsing with a slow soft glow against the fading stars.
Soft gold rims the dark hull as dawn breaks behind it, the ship vast and still, its own light kindling gently beneath.
A diffuse silver overcast fills the morning, the ship hanging in it like a thought, its edges barely distinguished from the sky.
The last stars fade slowly as a new light grows behind the visitor, something patient and immense announcing itself without sound.
A warm amber wash spills across the valley floor, the ship low and enormous above it, trailing its own pale inner glow.
Along the ship's curved underside a soft luminescence kindles, spreading panel by panel, each section brightening like an eye slowly opening.
The pre-dawn cold holds its blue silence while the hull begins to pulse, a slow silver breath moving across its darkened surface.
One clean shaft of white descends through layered mist, widening as it reaches earth, the surrounding air alive with suspended particles.
Dawn gold catches the upper rim of the dark hull, the rest of the ship still lost in the deep blue above.
A teal glow drifts outward through low fog, the source unseen but enormous, the meadow below holding its color like still water.
Silver overcast light flattens the world to grey, and within that grey the ship glows faintly, patient and self-contained and immense.
The amber sun climbs behind the arrival and pauses there, as if considering, the ship's silhouette burning soft at every edge.
Soft white light breathes along the hull in long slow pulses, each crest illuminating the underside before fading back to near dark.
The final stars dissolve as the sky lightens behind the visitor, their going quiet, the new light neither harsh nor entirely gentle.
A blue so cold and deep it feels ancient holds the ship in place, its belly lit from within by something warm.
Thin gold threads along the hull's lower edge where dawn first touches it, the rest of the vessel still wrapped in pre-dawn indigo.
White light falls in a single column to the open field, perfectly vertical, perfectly still, the grasses below bending softly in its warmth.
The mist glows teal for a long moment before the ship above it becomes visible, the light arriving before the source does.
Overcast silver presses evenly on the world, and the ship carries its own warmer glow within that grey, a diffuse amber presence.
Dawn rises slowly behind the arrival, lending its first light to the hull's rim while the belly still holds its own deep luminescence.
A pulsing soft luminescence moves across the hull in slow concentric rings, each one dimming before the next begins, the rhythm unhurried.
The ship hangs in the cold blue hour before sunrise, darker than the sky around it, its underside kindling to a quiet gold.
